text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back today, gaining 2.8%, after a rough week that saw the stock down nearly 7% since late October. The rebound aligns with broader strength in refining stocks—Chevron and Exxon hit all-time highs today as global diesel prices surged following attacks on refineries in Russia and the Middle East, which tightens fuel supply and lifts refining margins. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity, near peak utilization, which means MPC's operations benefit from this supply squeeze and higher prices for the products it makes.

The timing also matters: Marathon announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, which may have initially spooked the market, but the broader refining tailwinds—especially the jump in diesel prices globally—appear to be overriding concern about the internal shift. With US crude at $103 per barrel and world crude at $123, the gap between what refiners buy and what they sell (the refining margin) is widening, supporting profit potential for the company.
